column1: # One row per dispatched fleet member per run. DERIVED, NOT AUTHORED: every row
# is produced by plugin/scripts/member-outcomes.mjs from the harness's own
# subagent transcripts. Re-running the scraper REPLACES rows in place, and the
# whole file may be regenerated when the role classifier changes.
# NEVER hand-edit a row, and never add a column that a human must fill. A
# hand-entered value cannot survive a regeneration, which is exactly why the
# verdicts live in tier-outcomes.tsv instead. See
# BLANK MEANS UNKNOWN, never zero and never "no". `effort` is blank for models
# that carry no effort control; `ticket`/`pr` are blank when the member name
# does not identify one (merge-bot's number is a WAVE) and, for `pr`, the
# transcript shows no PR the member opened either. `subagent_type` and
# `ending` are the columns this rule does not cover — see their own
# WHERE `pr` COMES FROM. A PR-shaped name (`fix-pr-<n>`, `review-pr-<n>`,
# `finisher-<n>`, ...) carries it and wins. Otherwise — every implementer,
# whose `impl-<ticket>` name carries a ticket, never a PR — it is the PR the
# member's OWN `gh pr create` printed in its transcript (#2209): a `bash` call
# invoking `gh pr create`, whose result holds the PR URL on a line of its own.
# Blank when it opened none, when the create never printed its URL (a
# backgrounded call, gh's "already exists" refusal), or when it printed MORE
# than one distinct PR (a real one plus a throwaway probe) — never a guess.
# Only omp transcripts are read (ADR 0014), so every `harness=claude` row's
# `pr` stays as it was scraped: blank for every implementer there. Where an
# implementer's `pr` is filled, join a tier-outcomes.tsv verdict to it on `pr`,
# not `ticket`: a ticket dispatched more than once matches several rows.
# `agent` is an OPAQUE JOIN KEY — the member's transcript stem, relative to the
# session's subagents/ dir, used so a re-scrape REPLACES a row instead of
# duplicating it. It is not for display, not for grouping, and not domain data.
# Group on session, role, member and model. It is unique WITHIN A SESSION, which
# is all the key needs — it is NOT globally unique, because a NAMED member's
# stem is derived from its name and so repeats across sessions. Joining on
# `subagent_type` IS THE DISPATCH RECORD — what the member was dispatched AS,
# never what it called itself: Claude's meta.customAgentType, omp's
# session_init.agent, both read off the sidecar the scraper already opens, so
# it is DERIVED like every other column and survives a regeneration. The value
# is the bare definition name (`fleet-implementer-alt`), not the
# ITS BLANK IS NOT UNKNOWN, and what it records depends on the row's
# `harness`. On an omp row, blank means the transcript carried no
# `session_init` agent to read (no such line, or one without a string `agent`);
# an untyped dispatch is not that shape: omp records the generic `task` for it.
# On a claude row — scraped before the reader went omp-only (ADR 0014) and
# never re-scraped — blank means the sidecar carried no `customAgentType`,
# which Claude wrote only for a dispatch that named a type, so there blank IS
# an untyped dispatch. Every claude member dated before 2026-08-28 is blank,
# bar the typed `memory-housekeeper` and `memory-proxy` members, and 8,124 of
# 8,909 rows were blank as of 2026-09-12. That is a CLOSED category, not
# missing data: no re-scrape can ever fill it, and it can never hold a
# deliberate pair. Read as "unknown" it makes thousands of historical rows
# look like evidence waiting to be recovered.
# `ending` — HOW AN IMPLEMENTER'S RUN ENDED, read off its own transcript and
# the reports it wrote, never off a verdict. Values: `pr` (the row's `pr` is
# filled, its own `gh pr create` opened one — more than one leaves `pr` blank —
# or its last report names a PR an earlier same-ticket implementer
# opened); `bail:<cause>` (its last report bails: undecided, fork, hands, or
# covered); `bail:fixed` or `bail:fixed-refuted` (its bail says the work already
# reached main, and origin/main does or does not reach the sha it names);
# `provider` (a model fell back, or the last turn errored); `budget` (a budget
# notice reached it); `abort` (its last turn was aborted); `crash` (the session
# never exited and wrote no yield sidecar); `hollow` (none of the above: it
# stopped on its own); `unknown` (the transcript cannot say). A re-scrape that
# reads `unknown` keeps the ending the row already recorded: `unknown` is that
# scrape failing to say, such as an offline `verify-sha.sh`, never a reading.
# ITS BLANK IS NOT UNKNOWN: blank means the row is not an implementer, that is,
# its member's leaf is not `impl-<N>` with an optional retry suffix. A
# fix-applier booked `role=implementer` is blank here, because its member name
# TWO KNOWN LIMITS. Runs before reports were structured have no report to read,
# so a legitimate stop or continuation in them reads `hollow`. A member still
# running at the last scrape reads `crash` until the next scrape writes its
# transcript's real end. Claude-harness implementer rows read `unknown`, since
# no transcript is read for them.
# THE POPULATION IS BOTH TRANSCRIPT DEPTHS. A directly-dispatched member writes
# subagents/workflows/wf_<id>/agent-<id>.jsonl. Both are scraped, and the nested
# half is roughly as large as the flat one. It is mostly review specialists, and
# workflows/review-pr.js pins model: "sonnet" on three of its six dimensions —
# so it is where model VARIES. Filtering it out silently re-creates the sampling
# bug this file was corrected for.
# `dispatch_model` IS THE MODEL FIXED AT DISPATCH, where `model` is the
# member's LAST turn: omp's `session_init` model (`resolvedModel`, or the older
# `resolvedModelIdentity`) with its provider prefix and `:<level>` suffix
# member whose provider fell back mid-run keeps its dispatch model here while
# its `model` reads the fallback. Blank means unknown: the transcript carried
# no `session_init` model, or the row's session was no longer on disk when the
# column was added. Blank on every `harness=claude` row. Operator config
# SUPERSEDED GENERATIONS ARE A SEPARATE POPULATION. Rows carrying an older
# generation (claude-opus-4-7, claude-opus-4-8) must never be pooled with the
# current one under an "opus" label, and never read as a cheaper tier: pricing
# falls with each generation, so an older Opus is not cheaper than the current
# one and an older Sonnet is dearer. Pooling inverts the cost ordering this
# file exists to measure. The router's fit, the cost guard and the per-cell
# stopping rule therefore key a cell's figures on `dispatch_model`, never on
# `model`: each judges a cell on its newest dispatch model alone and reports
# the older ones beside it, never pooled.
# TOKEN COLUMNS ARE PER-TURN, folded on the transcript's message.id. One
# assistant turn is written as several jsonl lines, one per content block, each
# repeating the same usage object — so summing per LINE overcounted
# cache_creation by 176% and `turns` by 141%, unevenly across models. board.mjs
# folds the same way; the two must not drift apart. `tokens_out` is the max
# across a turn's lines, because output_tokens is a streaming snapshot.
# `cost` — are omp's per-turn usage, summed. `cost` is Σ usage.cost.total, the
# provider's own TTL-aware figure and the $ of record; pricing.json beside this
# file only cross-checks it from the token columns and never produces a $ of its
# (usage.cttl.ephemeral1h); the 5m share is the difference. All four are blank
# on every `harness=claude` row, which no reader re-scrapes, and blank on an omp
# row whose transcript recorded no such figure.
# `report` — whether the member left its report file in the scratch root — is
# DERIVED like the rest, from the member's name and the file system, never from
# exists and does not), `absent` (no such file), `-` for a member no schema
# covers (specialists, memory members, review runners). It is blank only where
# the scraper found no scratch root to look in, and then only for a member a
# schema covers. The value is the state of the file WHEN THE ROW WAS LAST
# SCRAPED: plugin/scripts/reclaim-scratch.mjs removes a report with its member's
# PR or ticket, so a re-scrape after that reads `absent`, and a member's name
# repeats across sessions, so a file under that name is read on every row that
# bears it. `absent` on a row older than report files means no file, never that
# the member failed to write one.
# There is no `errored` column. Transcript torn-ness is a property of WHEN the
# scraper ran, not of the member — it flips back on the next re-scrape — so it
# is reported on stderr and never stored. A member that stalled or hit a
# terminal API failure leaves a syntactically complete file and is
# indistinguishable here. Whether the work was any good is a verdict, and
# verdicts live in tier-outcomes.tsv, joined on `pr`.
# A CELL'S COMPARISONS — the only unconfounded comparison — are counted by
# plugin/scripts/cell-readout.mjs, not by a query in this header. A Pull is a
# ticket-features.tsv row, joined to its row here on `session`+`agent`; its
# `chosen_cell` names the cell. For a cell X other than slow-high, a comparison
# is one session holding an ADMISSIBLE row at X and an admissible slow-high row
# whose resolved (`model`, `effort`) differ from the X row's. A row is
# and its `effort` is the cell's level — so no `fleet-implementer` or
# `fleet-implementer-alt` row from before the cell grid is any cell's
# comparison. A cell is read only once it has at least ten comparisons across
# five or more distinct `run_date`s, this file's own `run_date`:
# prints `<cell> <comparisons> <run_dates> <resolved models>` for each cell past
# that gate — `mixed (<model-a> n=…, <model-b> n=…)` when the cell's admissible
# rows span more than one model — and nothing that identifies a comparison,
# because run-team's gate forbids reading them early.
# Both sides are named by the DISPATCH, never by the role classifier, and
# never by "these two models differ" alone. The role classifier cannot name a
# side at all: every implementer definition books `role=implementer`. Until
# #1486 it failed the other way on omp — a fleet implementer booked
# `role=other` there, so a role filter dropped that harness outright — and that
# a DERIVED classification moved under the query at all is the standing reason
# the key is the dispatch record instead. #1066: the session+role+model query
# the pre-cell pair query replaced counted every session that happened to stage
# a routine ticket beside a correction one. Measured 2026-09-12 on this corpus:
# 198 keys as that query was written, 35 sessions across 21 run_dates once
# restricted to implementers, against 17 real pairs across 8.
# The resolved test stays, on TOP of the dispatch test. Measured 2026-09-12: one
# omp session dispatched 12 alt and 15 top implementers that all resolved to
# claude-sonnet-5 anyway (a modelRoles override upstream of the dispatch), so
# the intent was deliberate and the comparison empty. Counting intent alone
# read 18 pairs across 9 run_dates where 17 across 8 was the truth.
